university: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center

documents.unit: Chief Information Officer / AI Governance and Risk Committee
documents.title: HSC OP 52.21, Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools
documents.summary: An operating policy for the whole health sciences center covering education, research, clinical care and administration. It allows AI use under principles of disclosure, accountability, privacy and human supervision, bans AI on protected data without a contract, and sets up a governance committee. Coursework rules are thin: academic work is limited only where the instructor disallows AI.
documents.stance_why: The policy does not ban AI: it sets conditions, e.g. "AI use must be disclosed and documented appropriately" and public data "may be used freely with AI tools". Prohibited uses are narrow (unvetted tools with confidential data, grading, "completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor"), so the stance is permit with conditions, not restrict or delegates.

units.why: The purpose statement sets scope and principles: 'responsible, ethical, and compliant use' of AI across education, research, clinical care and administration. That is an institution-wide framework, so P56.
units.anchor: establish clear expectations and guidelines for the responsible, ethical, and compliant use of artificial intelligence

units.why: The review clause says the OP 'will be reviewed by March 1 of each odd-numbered year', a fixed review cycle, so P54.
units.anchor: will be reviewed by March 1 of each odd-numbered year

units.why: Names the officers who review the OP: 'Chief Information Officer and the Chief Compliance Officer', with revisions forwarded to a committee. This says who maintains the policy, so P80; the review cycle itself is coded separately as P54.
units.anchor: by the Chief Information Officer and the Chief Compliance Officer

units.why: Defines AI tools as software that uses 'machine learning (ML), natural language processing, large language models', setting what the policy covers, so P61.
units.anchor: software, systems, or applications that use machine learning (ML), natural language processing, large language models

units.why: The exclusions list says 'basic rule-based spell/grammar checkers' are not AI tools. P100 is the nearest type (routine features outside the rules), though here the reason is that they are not AI.
units.anchor: basic rule-based spell/grammar checkers, simple macros, mail-merge
units.fit_note: Exclusion is because the tools are not AI (deterministic), not an exemption of AI features from a restrictive rule.

units.why: Boundary rule: a feature advertising 'AI,' 'smart,' 'assist,' or 'predictive' capabilities is in scope 'even if the larger product would otherwise be excluded'. It extends the rules to embedded AI features, so P07.
units.anchor: those capabilities are in scope even if the larger product would otherwise be excluded
units.fit_note: Covers embedded AI features in general software (predictive text, ML analytics), not only editors and IDEs.

units.why: 'Vendor updates that add AI capabilities bring that product or feature into scope' extends coverage to AI added later to existing products, so P07.
units.anchor: Vendor updates that add AI capabilities bring that product or feature into scope
units.fit_note: About vendor updates adding AI to existing products rather than editors and IDEs specifically.

units.why: 'When in doubt, treat the feature as an AI tool' and consult the committee. It tells users what to do when unsure, so P10, though it routes to a committee rather than an instructor.
units.anchor: When in doubt, treat the feature as an AI tool
units.fit_note: Unsure users treat the feature as in scope and consult the AI Governance and Risk Committee, not an instructor.

units.why: States the rationale as ensuring responsible use as AI is integrated: 'it's essential to use these technologies responsibly'. Framework preamble, so P56.
units.anchor: With the increasing integration of AI tools into university activities

units.why: Transparency principle: 'AI use must be disclosed and documented appropriately', a general disclosure duty for any user, so P24.
units.anchor: AI use must be disclosed and documented appropriately

units.why: Documentation 'should include the type of AI tool used, its purpose, and any limitations', specifying what a disclosure contains. P25 (tool details) is the nearest type, though no prompt or output is required.
units.anchor: Documentation should include the type of AI tool used, its purpose, and any limitations
units.fit_note: Requires tool type, purpose and limitations; no prompt or output required.

units.why: Accountability principle: 'Human users have final responsibility for all decisions and outcomes resulting from AI use', so users own what AI helps produce, P29.
units.anchor: Human users have final responsibility for all decisions and outcomes resulting from AI use
units.fit_note: Responsibility for decisions and outcomes, framed for all users, not student submissions specifically.

units.why: 'Users must evaluate AI outputs, recognize the tool's limitations, and take corrective action if AI-generated results are inaccurate' requires verification of output, so P31.
units.anchor: Users must evaluate AI outputs, recognize the tool

units.why: Fairness principle: AI 'must be used in ways that uphold fair treatment of all individuals and avoid discrimination', so bias and harms, P53.
units.anchor: uphold fair treatment of all individuals and avoid discrimination

units.why: Privacy principle: 'AI use must protect sensitive, confidential, and personally identifiable information', so P50.
units.anchor: AI use must protect sensitive, confidential, and personally identifiable information

units.why: 'Data input into AI systems should be minimized to only what is necessary for the task' is a separate data-minimization rule, so P50.
units.anchor: Data input into AI systems should be minimized to only what is necessary
units.frag_end: to prevent unauthorized access or breaches.

units.why: Human supervision principle: AI 'is intended as a decision-support tool, not a replacement for human judgment', so humans remain the decision-makers, P32.
units.anchor: AI is intended as a decision-support tool, not a replacement for human judgment
units.fit_note: Frames AI as decision support for all users, not about students' own problem-solving.

units.why: 'All outputs must be subject to human review, with the capacity to override or modify' AI recommendations. P73 (a human reviews and decides) fits best.
units.anchor: All outputs must be subject to human review, with the capacity to override or modify
units.fit_note: Human review of all AI outputs, especially in high-risk academic, research and clinical decisions; not limited to decisions about individuals.

units.why: 'The AI Governance and Risk Committee is established by the President's Cabinet to provide strategic and operational oversight', naming the owning body, so P80.
units.anchor: provide strategic and operational oversight for all AI-related activities

units.why: Lists committee membership including 'Faculty and Student Representatives (optional)', describing how the governing body is composed. P84 is nearest; it describes composition, not how the policy was drafted.
units.anchor: Faculty and Student Representatives (optional)
units.fit_note: Describes committee composition rather than how the policy was drafted or adopted.

units.why: The committee must 'Approve and maintain AI policies, procedures, and standards', assigning policy maintenance to a body, so P80.
units.anchor: Approve and maintain AI policies, procedures, and standards.

units.why: The committee must 'Review and approve proposed AI tools and high-risk projects across clinical, research, education, and administrative domains', tool approval, so P65.
units.anchor: Review and approve proposed AI tools and high-risk projects

units.why: The committee must 'Assess risk, including privacy, security, bias, and ethical considerations', part of tool review, so P65.
units.anchor: Assess risk, including privacy, security, bias, and ethical considerations.

units.why: The committee must 'Monitor AI system performance and compliance post-deployment', ongoing monitoring of deployed systems, so P98.
units.anchor: Monitor AI system performance and compliance post-deployment.

units.why: The committee must 'Evaluate vendor partnerships and contracts for AI solutions', contract review, so P65.
units.anchor: Evaluate vendor partnerships and contracts for AI solutions.

units.why: The committee must 'Oversee training programs and competency requirements for AI users', so training for users, P70.
units.anchor: Oversee training programs and competency requirements for AI users.

units.why: The committee must 'Receive and review reports of incidents or concerns; recommend mitigation and corrective actions', an incident channel, so P71.
units.anchor: Receive and review reports of incidents or concerns

units.why: 'Public Data may be used freely with AI tools' is a permissive rule for public data. P02 is closest, though it applies only to one data class.
units.anchor: Public Data may be used freely with AI tools
units.fit_note: Permission applies only to public data; it is a data-handling rule, not a general default stance.

units.why: 'Sensitive, Controlled, and Regulated Data can be used with AI tools that are managed by TTUHSC and covered by contracts', i.e. only vetted tools for protected data, so P50.
units.anchor: can be used with AI tools that are managed by TTUHSC and covered by contracts

units.why: 'AI tools should be used as decision-support tools and not as decision- making tools' bars AI from deciding, so P73.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used as decision-support tools and not as decision-
units.fit_note: General rule for decisions, not specifically decisions about individuals.

units.why: 'use should be consistent with the HSC OP 52.09 ... and HSC OP 56.01' ties AI use to existing confidentiality and IT acceptable-use policies, so P77.
units.anchor: In all cases, use should be consistent with the
units.frag_end: Acceptable Use of Information Technology Resources

units.why: 'Users may use only the information and information systems to which they have been given authorized access', with a confidentiality duty, a privacy rule, so P50.
units.anchor: Users may use only the information and information systems to which they have

units.why: 'AI tools that lack a TTUHSC contract and appropriate data- sharing safeguards are not approved' for protected data, so unvetted tools are barred, P50.
units.anchor: AI tools that lack a TTUHSC contract and appropriate data- sharing safeguards are not approved

units.why: 'AI tools may not be used with personal, confidential, proprietary, or other sensitive information unless a contract' protects it, naming FERPA student records, so P50.
units.anchor: AI tools may not be used with personal, confidential, proprietary, or other sensitive information

units.why: Among non-public outputs AI should not generate is 'completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor'. It forbids AI-completed work only where the instructor disallows it, so P19, with the instructor deciding.
units.anchor: completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor
units.frag_start: AI tools should not be used
units.fit_note: Bans AI completing academic work only where the instructor disallows it; the instructor sets the rule (P04) and the policy gives no tiers or default for coursework.

units.why: The same list bars AI from 'grading'. Grades are meant to be assigned by humans, so P46 rather than P101 (no conditions are given).
units.anchor: creation of non-public instructional materials; and grading.
units.frag_start: AI tools should not be used

units.why: The list bars AI for 'creation of non-public instructional materials', limiting instructor AI use for teaching work, so P59.
units.anchor: creation of non-public instructional materials
units.frag_start: AI tools should not be used

units.why: The list bars AI for 'recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision making', consequential decisions about people, so P73.
units.anchor: recruitment, personnel, or disciplinary decision making
units.frag_start: AI tools should not be used

units.why: The list bars 'generating proprietary or unpublished research' with AI, a research-use restriction, so P62.
units.anchor: generating proprietary or unpublished research
units.frag_start: AI tools should not be used

units.why: AI 'must not be used for activities that are illegal, fraudulent, or violate any state or federal laws', a general conduct ban, so P74.
units.anchor: AI tools must not be used for activities that are illegal, fraudulent

units.why: 'Accepting click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may result in personal responsibility' warns about AI tools' terms of use, nearest P52.
units.anchor: accepting click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may result in personal responsibility
units.frag_end: terms and conditions of the AI tool.
units.fit_note: Concerns personal liability from terms of use, not copyright or ownership.

units.why: 'Contact TTUHSC IT before purchasing (or acquiring for free) AI tools' requires pre-acquisition review, so P65.
units.anchor: Contact TTUHSC IT before purchasing (or acquiring for free) AI tools
units.frag_end: resources or data will be used.
units.fit_note: Individual users must contact IT before acquiring; an obligation on users rather than a committee review.

units.why: 'Do not input Personal Information about TTUHSC employees, students, faculty, or other stakeholders into an AI tool unless explicitly allowed' is a data-protection ban, so P50.
units.anchor: Do not input Personal Information about TTUHSC employees, students, faculty, or other stakeholders

units.why: 'Users must adhere to the terms and conditions of AI tools and protect intellectual property rights', covering copyright and patent, so P52.
units.anchor: Users must adhere to the terms and conditions of AI tools and protect intellectual

units.why: 'Many digital resources provided by TTUHSC Libraries are subject to vendor licenses that may restrict AI use'; users should ask Libraries. Licensed content may not be freely given to AI, nearest P49.
units.anchor: subject to vendor licenses that may restrict AI use
units.fit_note: Advises contacting Libraries about licensed content, not an outright ban on uploading.

units.why: 'Always confirm the accuracy of AI-generated information before relying on it', since outputs 'may be inaccurate, biased, or fabricated', so P31.
units.anchor: Always confirm the accuracy of AI-generated information before relying on it.

units.why: 'Users are responsible for any published content that incorporates AI-generated material' makes users own what they publish, so P29.
units.anchor: Users are responsible for any published content that incorporates AI-generated material

units.why: 'Clearly disclose when written materials or other work products are generated with or derived from AI tools' is a disclosure rule, so P24.

units.why: 'Do not use AI tools to create malicious content, including malware, viruses, worms, or trojan horses', a conduct ban, so P74.
